subject: Staggered incentive onramp & billing handoff — OpalWorks renewal
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@opalworks.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staggered incentive onramp & billing handoff — OpalWorks renewal

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for taking time last week — excited about OpalWorks' plans to scale search and recommendations across your storefronts next year. Per our call, I pulled together a proposal that blends a short-term volume incentive with a multi-quarter billing cadence to smooth cashflow on your side while preserving unit economics for Redwood.

High level:
- 6-month staggered onramp: tiered credit offsets for months 1–3 (40% credit on incremental tokens), months 4–6 (20%).
- Price hold for 12 months on the baseline unit rate if OpalWorks commits to the attached 12-month minimum consumption (we can discuss a monthly true-up).
- Optional burst pool (pay-as-you-go) for spikes above committed throughput; early-access discount for self-serve embedding endpoints.

I attached a simple schedule (OpalWorks_incentive_schedule_v1.xlsx) that shows the credit math and sample invoices. A few asks from my side:
1) Can you confirm whether you prefer a single quarterly invoice or monthly invoices with a quarterly true-up?
2) Is legal open to an abbreviated amendment (1–2 pages) that references the existing SOW and specifies the credit schedule?

If that sounds reasonable, I can loop finance and contracts and send a draft amendment for signature.

Short note: If you need the credits front-loaded instead of spread, we can trade shorter price hold or a slightly higher baseline rate. Happy to model both.

Thanks,
Lukas

--
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
l.meyer@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: OpalWorks_incentive_schedule_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@opalworks.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staggered incentive onramp & billing handoff — OpalWorks renewal

Thanks Lukas — this reads well and aligns with what I outlined to our CFO. A couple quick clarifications:

- Billing cadence: CFO prefers monthly invoices (for our accounting cadence) with a quarterly reconciliation/true-up. Is that straightforward for Redwood?
- Credits: frontline engineering suggested front-loading more credit in month 1 (we expect a heavy test & tuning month). Can we shift to 60% credit in month 1, 30% in month 2, 10% in month 3 and then the 20% step for months 4–6?
- Legal: Rajesh (cc'd) will review the short amendment. He asked us to keep any termination/true-up language minimal — we can accept the price hold language if the baseline is clearly defined.

If you can send a draft amendment and an example invoice flow (monthly invoice + quarterly true-up example) that would help us get internal approvals next week.

Appreciate the flexibility — Olivia

--
Olivia Park
Head of Platform, OpalWorks
olivia.park@opalworks.com | +1 312-555-0922
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Staggered incentive onramp & billing handoff — OpalWorks renewal

Ben / Vanessa — forwarding Olivia's reply. Quick asks:

1) Finance ops: can we support monthly invoices + quarterly true-up for OpalWorks? They want month-1 heavier credit (60/30/10 then 20/20/0 for months 4–6). That would materially shift our short-term revenue recognition — can we do it if we treat the credits as bill-back (contra revenue) rather than pre-funded credits?

2) Contracts: Olivia asked for an abbreviated amendment. Attached is a docx template I started (Redwood_Amendment_v2.docx). We should keep termination/true-up language tight — can legal approve a 2-page amendment that references the current T&Cs and includes: baseline definition, credit schedule table, invoice cadence, and a 12-month price hold on the baseline?

3) Risk: do we want the optional condition that if they underconsume baseline for two consecutive quarters we reserve the right to re-open pricing? That was proposed internally as a safety valve. Thoughts?

Attachment: Redwood_Amendment_v2.docx (draft amendment, 2 pages)

Pls reply with short bullets so I can get back to Olivia this afternoon.

Thanks — Lukas
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@opalworks.com>
Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh@opalworks.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staggered incentive onramp & billing handoff — OpalWorks renewal

Olivia / Rajesh — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per internal check-in, Redwood can accommodate your requested cadence and front-loaded credit structure with these guardrails:

Summary of agreed terms (draft):
- Billing: Monthly invoices with quarterly reconciliation (OpalWorks invoices paid monthly; Redwood issues a quarterly true-up credit or additional charge as needed).
- Credit schedule (applies to incremental consumption above prior baseline during onramp): Month 1 = 60% credit, Month 2 = 30% credit, Month 3 = 10% credit, Months 4–6 = 20% credit per month on incremental usage.
- Price hold: 12 months on the defined baseline unit rate (baseline = average monthly consumption over prior 3 billing months, as noted in amendment).
- Recognition/ops: Finance will treat these credits as contra revenue applied at the time of the quarterly reconciliation; this enables monthly invoices without pre-funding.
- Safety valve: If OpalWorks consumes below the baseline for two consecutive quarters, either party may request a commercial review. This is intended as a mutual-review clause, not immediate repricing.

Next steps:
1) I attached a revised amendment draft (Redwood_Amendment_v2.docx) with the table above and a sample invoice flow.
2) We will post the amendment to DocuSign once legal confirms wording (link: https://www.docusign.com/Amendment/OPW-342).
3) Ben / Vanessa — please confirm offline if any billing system/cashflow gotchas remain; otherwise I will send the DocuSign package to OpalWorks tonight.

Olivia — if that matches your expectations I’ll route the DocuSign with the amendment + example invoice and we can aim to finalize before your CFO sync on Friday.

Best,
Lukas

--
